title: Heartbeat admission lease failover to rescue dispatcher stalls and long-context tail
creator: Ethan Park
description: Summary: We received three customer escalations (Hosted: low, Dedicated: high, Private: high) describing periodic p99+/tail latency spikes correlated with long-context sequences. Investigation pointed to a rare dispatcher stall where admission leases for short/latency-sensitive requests were not being renewed under mixed-length waves, causing queue starvation for small requests and batch amplification for long requests. Root cause hypothesis: an instance-level admission lease state was allowed to lapse when the heartbeat renewal path raced with a KV cache compaction event and an internal prefetch quarantine, producing a transient token that left the admission window closed until the next scheduler tick.
acceptance_criteria: Can reproduce regression in lab with mixed-length synthetic traffic and a KV compaction event
Heartbeat-driven lease renewals prevent short-request starvation under bursty long-sequence waves in 10k request/min synthetic harness
Canary rollout shows p99 drop to baseline on Dedicated and Private clusters over 72h
No regression in throughput for long-context workloads (<=2% throughput variance)
Automated test added to scheduler integration suite simulating heartbeat loss + compaction
implementation_notes: Add per-instance heartbeat lease with monotonic generation counter. Heartbeat renewals occur on admission path and on watchdog timer failure path.
Make lease renewal resilient to KV compaction by reading generation from an atomic metadata key rather than in-memory ephemeral state.
Introduce short grace-window (50ms) on admission decision to accept pending short requests when a renewal is in-flight to avoid head-of-line starvation.
Patch: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/8421 (adds lease+watchdog), follow-up PR #8426 for tests and metrics
Feature-flag gated: SCHED_HEARTBEAT_LEASE=true for canary rollout
testing_plan: Unit tests for lease generation/renewal and race conditions
Integration test in CI: mixed-length arrival stream with randomized KV compaction triggers
Load lab canary: Dedicated cluster with production-like traffic (10% long-context, 90% short), 72h run
Private customer patch deployment with rollback plan and instrumentation hook for immediate disable via console
Compare metrics: admission-failures, batch-size-distribution, p50/p95/p99, kv-cache-hit-rate, scheduler-tick-latency
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-cluster admission window occupancy, short-request queue depth, batch amplification ratio
Runbook: if lease_renewal_failure_rate spikes, toggle SCHED_HEARTBEAT_LEASE=false and scale up scheduler replicas as a mitigation
rollout_plan: Stage 1: internal canary on staging (SCHED_HEARTBEAT_LEASE=true) — validate synthetic harness (48h)
Stage 2: small Dedicated canary (5% hosts) for customers flagged by support (72h)
Stage 3: widen to 25% Dedicated + Private test clusters if metrics stable (72h)
Stage 4: full rollout to Hosted with gradual traffic ramp and close monitoring
Rollback criteria: p99 increases >10% vs baseline, or lease_renewal_failure_rate >1%
